...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon (US 41) has been steadily
rising since July and on September 15, reached flood stage. The cause
of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is
excessive hydrilla growth (from river bottom to the water surface)
along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.
The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing
water levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM EDT Thursday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 28.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3
feet on 10/05/1965.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

properties.areaDesc: Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 16 at 2:03PM AKDT until September 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. Showers will continue through the
end of the week, with the bulk of the rainfall expected through
Thursday morning. Storm total rainfall during this time will be
around 0.50" to 1.00". It has been very wet lately and this
amount of rain has the potential to bring the Chena and Little
Chena Rivers above minor flood stage beginning Thursday afternoon
into Friday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding through the end of the week as water
levels gradually rise then fall. In addition, while we are not
expecting much flooding away from rivers, streams and creeks, as
the ground is already saturated and may struggle to hold more
water. This can lead to pooling and ponding of water across the
area which may make travel difficult in localized spots.

- There is some uncertainty with exact timing and amounts of
rainfall but as details become clearer, we will continue to
update.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor the latest forecasts and be alert for possible
Flood Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 16 at 11:35AM AKDT until September 17 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River
drainage in combination with excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Lower Kuskokwim including Napakiak, Napaskiak, Oscarville,
Bethel, and Kwethluk.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1130 AM AKDT Wednesday, the river gauge at Bethel indicates
water levels above flood stage, at or above 8.5 ft. Additionally,
reports out of the Lower Kuskokwim, including Napakiak,
Napaskiak, Oscarville, Bethel and Kwethluk, confirm flooding in
low-lying areas. Water levels may drop with the outgoing tide
this (Wednesday) afternoon, but are expected to rise again
Thursday morning with another high tide cycle.

These high water levels are a result of the Kuskokwim River
back-up at its outlet in combination with heavy rain runoff
farther upstream. Minor flooding will continue from overflow of
poor drainage areas. High tides will decrease later in the week,
allowing the backwater of the Kuskokwim River to drain, lowering
water levels to below flood stage.
- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:
At 11:30am Wednesday the reading was 8.9 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.
At 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown
Slough and flood low lying areas.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

If you live near or along Kuskokwim stay alert and be prepared to
take action.
